issues.legal_issue: A junior family member has no right to partition an ancestral estate made impartible by grant and succession under primogeniture, although a right of succession may continue unless renounced.
material_facts: A permanent grant provided for enjoyment and succession from generation to generation.
The estate passed through successive generations to the eldest male descendant under primogeniture.
The junior family member received maintenance from the estate and sought a partition share.
There was no evidence that the junior family member had expressly or by implication renounced a right of succession.
issues.conclusion: The estate was indivisible and impartible, devolving on the eldest lineal descendant under primogeniture; the junior family member was not entitled to a partition share in it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mitakshara law as modified by the custom of impartibility, an impartible estate is not subject to partition or ordinary joint enjoyment, while the right of survivorship may remain. Renunciation of that succession right must be proved to establish that the family has ceased to be joint for purposes of succession. The Court relied on Baijnath Prasad Singh v. Tej Bali Singh, Katama Natchiar v. Raja of Shivganga, Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, Chinnathayi v. Kulasekara Pandiya Naicker, and Anant Bhikkappa Patil v. Shankar Ramchandra Patil.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.ancestral_impartible_grant: The property was an ancestral estate granted or held as indivisible and impartible.
predicates.primogeniture_succession: The estate passed to the eldest male lineal descendant under a rule of primogeniture.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding concerns an ancestral impartible estate that passes by primogeniture, the junior family member has no partition share in the estate.

issues.legal_issue: Income from an impartible estate belongs to its holder and does not become joint family income merely because junior family members are entitled to maintenance or may later succeed.
material_facts: The junior family member received maintenance from the estate’s income.
The holder’s possession of the estate gave rise to the maintenance entitlement.
The income was not jointly enjoyed by the holder and the junior family member.
issues.conclusion: The income and its accumulations were the absolute property of the holder, not income of the undivided family.
issues.legal_principle: The income of an impartible estate is the holder’s income, not joint family income; a maintenance right does not make the recipient a co-owner of that income. The Court relied on Jagdamba Kumari v. Wazir Narain, Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras v. Hon’ble Sri Ravu Swetachalapati Ramakrishna Ranga Rao, and Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.income_from_impartible_estate: The income at issue was derived from an estate held as impartible.

issues.definition: If a partition proceeding concerns income derived from an impartible estate, that income belongs to the estate’s holder.

issues.legal_issue: Immovable property acquired by the holder may become part of an impartible estate when the holder intended to incorporate it into that estate.
material_facts: Additional lands were acquired from income derived from the impartible estate.
The properties were treated as incorporated into the estate, and the Court found them to be part of it.
The properties were claimed as divisible family property.
issues.conclusion: The acquired lands found to have been incorporated into the estate were part of the impartible estate and were not partible.
issues.legal_principle: Incorporation of immovable property into an impartible estate depends on the holder’s intention, which may be express or inferred from conduct and treatment of the property. Income from the estate does not by itself make an acquisition part of the estate. The Court relied on Smt. Rani Prabha Kumari Dibi v. Jagdish Chunder Dhabal, Janki Pershad Singh v. Dwarka Pershad Singh, Murtaza Husain Khan v. Mohd. Yasin Ali Khan, Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, and Mirza Raja Shri Pushavathi Viziaram Gajapathi Raj v. Shri Pushavathi Visweswar Gajapathi Raj.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.immovable_property_acquired_by_estate_ho: The holder of an impartible estate acquired immovable property.
predicates.holder_intended_incorporation: The holder’s intention to incorporate the acquired property into the estate was shown by express evidence or by the holder’s conduct and treatment of it.

issues.definition: When an estate holder acquires immovable property and intends to incorporate it into the estate, the acquired property is part of the impartible estate.

issues.legal_issue: An ancestral family residence outside the impartible grant, together with accretions not shown to have been held separately, remains partible joint family property.
material_facts: The ancestral residence was not covered by the grant of the impartible estate.
The family members lived in the residence.
Improvements and accretions were made to the residence, including with income from the estate.
There was no evidence that the holders treated the residence or its accretions as separate property, or that the junior family member gave up a share in them.
issues.conclusion: The ancestral residence and its accretions were joint family property and the decree for partition of those properties was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Property outside an impartible grant may remain ordinary joint family property. Accretions to ancestral joint family property remain joint unless shown to have been treated as separate property; a junior member’s interest is not lost without evidence of express or implied relinquishment.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and ancestral_residence_outside_grant and family_jointly_used_residence and no_separate_treatment_of_accretions

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.ancestral_residence_outside_grant: The family residence was ancestral and was not included in the impartible grant.
predicates.family_jointly_used_residence: The family members lived together in the residence.
predicates.no_separate_treatment_of_accretions: There was no evidence that the holders treated additions to the residence as separate property.

issues.definition: An ancestral residence outside an impartible grant that the family jointly used, with no separate treatment of its accretions, is partible.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation paid for resumed lands of an impartible estate retains the impartible character of the estate.
material_facts: Lands forming part of the impartible estate were resumed under the abolition legislation.
Compensation was paid in lieu of those lands to the holder of the estate.
A junior family member claimed a share of the compensation.
issues.conclusion: The compensation retained the impartible character of the estate, and the junior family member had no share in it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 18 of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagir Act, 1951, the resumption concerned the Jagir lands and compensation was payable to the Jagirdar in lieu of those lands. Compensation in place of an impartible estate retains its impartible character. The Court also relied on Ravi Janardhana Krishna Ranga Rao v. State of Madras.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property or related compensation.
predicates.compensation_paid_for_resumed_impartible: Compensation was paid in place of lands resumed from an impartible estate.

issues.definition: When compensation is paid for lands resumed from an impartible estate, the compensation retains the estate’s impartible character.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory tenancy rights conferred on the holder of retained agricultural lands devolve under the applicable tenancy law rather than becoming divisible merely because the Jagir was abolished.
material_facts: The Jagir was abolished and the holder was declared a pucca tenant of retained Khudkhast lands.
The applicable land-revenue legislation conferred tenancy rights on the holder.
The Court held that the relevant lands became the properties of the holder’s successors.
issues.conclusion: The specified retained lands became the properties of the appellants through succession to the holder’s statutory tenancy rights.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied sections 19 of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagir Act, 1951, and sections 54(7), 69 and 82 of the Madhya Bharat Land Revenue and Tenancy Act, 1950, and referred to sections 158(1)(b) and 164 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code. It relied on Anant Kibe v. Purushottam Rao for the effect of statutory tenancy rights on the former incidents of impartibility and primogeniture.

predicates.proceeding_claiming_share_in_retained_la: A family member brought a proceeding claiming a share in agricultural land retained after abolition of an estate.
predicates.holder_received_statutory_tenancy_rights: The former estate holder received tenancy rights in retained agricultural land under the applicable legislation.
predicates.successor_inherits_holder_rights: The claimant is a successor to the holder of those statutory tenancy rights.

issues.definition: When retained land is held under statutory tenancy rights that pass to a successor, the land belongs to that successor under the applicable succession to tenancy rights.

issues.legal_issue: Movable property does not become part of an impartible estate merely because it was acquired from estate income, unless a family custom or other sufficient evidence establishes its incorporation.
material_facts: The disputed jewellery and utensils were movable property.
There was no finding of a family custom treating the movables as part of the estate’s regalia.
The junior family member had received jewellery at marriage.
The movables were claimed for partition.
issues.conclusion: The jewellery and utensils were personal property and were not liable to partition.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of incorporation ordinarily applies to immovable property, not movables; movables may form part of an impartible estate if a family custom or other sufficient evidence establishes that result. The Court relied on Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi and Mirza Raja Shri Pushavathi Viziaram Gajapathi Raj v. Shri Pushavathi Visweswar Gajapathi Raj.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.disputed_property_is_movable: The property claimed for partition consists of movable items.
predicates.no_custom_or_evidence_of_incorporation: No family custom or other sufficient evidence shows that the movables were incorporated into the impartible estate.

issues.definition: Movable property claimed in a partition proceeding is not partible as estate property when there is no custom or other sufficient evidence of its incorporation into the impartible estate.

issues.legal_issue: A junior family member who has already received maintenance is not entitled to an additional share of a family cash grant solely by reason of junior membership.
material_facts: A cash grant was made to the family.
The junior family member had already received maintenance as a junior member of the family.
The junior family member claimed an additional share of the cash grant.
issues.conclusion: The junior family member was not entitled to a share of the cash grant, and the partition decree concerning it was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the cash grant as belonging to the family and held that the junior member’s maintenance entitlement, already received, did not create a further right to share in that grant.

predicates.partition_proceeding: A family member brought a proceeding seeking partition of property or a family grant.
predicates.cash_grant_made_to_family: The cash grant was made to the family.
predicates.junior_member_already_received_maintenan: The junior family member had already received maintenance from the family.

issues.definition: A junior family member who has already received maintenance has no additional share in a cash grant made to the family.
